findings.observation: There is one caption line, centred horizontally, with its baseline about 78% down the frame. It sits in the same spot in every shot, whatever the background. The top ~70% is left clear for the picture and the bottom ~20% for platform UI.
findings.rule: Put captions on a single centred line at about 75–80% of frame height. Never move them between shots. Keep the top area and the bottom ~20% free of text.
findings.measured: Caption y ≈ 242/310 px of tile height (≈78%) on overview tiles S1–S18 and every S11 burst frame
findings.evidence: Overview S1–S18; S11 f266–f281; S12 f284–f313

findings.observation: Captions are small white bold sans-serif in plain sentence case, as spoken. There is no box or outline, only a soft dark drop shadow. Line width changes with the words and never fills the frame. A 2-word chunk is about 30% of frame width; a 4-word chunk is about 70%. Letter height is about 3% of frame height.
findings.rule: Use a small white bold sans with a soft dark drop shadow and no background box. Keep the type small enough that a 4-word line covers no more than ~70% of the frame width.
findings.measured: 'bites you' ≈56/176 px tile width (32%); 'six needle like tools' ≈122/176 (69%)

findings.observation: Captions show a short phrase of 2–4 words, about 3 on average. Punctuation and hyphens are removed ('needle like', 'Next a hollow blade'). Compound words are split into normal spellings ('horse fly'). There are no colour or scale changes for emphasis.
findings.rule: Break the narration into 2–4 word phrases. Remove punctuation and hyphens. Give every word the same colour and size, with no highlight words.

findings.observation: Chunks hard-swap with no pop, fade or scale animation. A chunk can show up about 1 frame before its first word starts or a few frames after. One chunk stays up across several fast cuts: 'six needle like tools' lasts through S4–S8, about 1.8 s and 5 shots. 'open like scissors' carries across the S10→S11 cut.
findings.rule: Swap caption chunks with a hard cut, within 0–3 frames of the first word of the phrase. Don't animate them. Let a chunk stay up across picture cuts so the text stays calm while the images change fast.
findings.measured: 'while two more' visible f284, 'while' starts f285; 'have tiny teeth' appears f306, 'have' starts f303 (+3 f)
findings.evidence: S12 f284–f313; S11 f266–f281; overview S4–S8

findings.observation: There are no explainer graphics: no labels, arrows, icons, highlight boxes or maps. Every fact is shown by the 3D render itself, for example a macro close-up of the part being named. The only overlay is the caption.
findings.rule: Show each fact with the animated scene: cut or push in to the object as it is named. Don't use labels or diagram overlays. Captions are the only layer drawn on top.
findings.evidence: All 18 overview tiles; S11, S12 bursts

findings.observation: White text stays readable on bright cyan sky, peach skin and saturated red tissue, using only the drop shadow. The text colour never changes with the background.
findings.rule: Use one caption colour for the whole video. Rely on the shadow for contrast rather than changing the colour or adding a box for each scene.
